faqs.question: Where can I find everything I need as a new student?
alternatives: I'm a new student, where do I start?
first year student getting started guide
what should I do first when I start at CDU
faqs.answer:
The best place to start is the **New to CDU** page. It walks you through activating your account, enrolling, setting up IT and getting your timetable.

If you'd like one-on-one help with account activation, enrolment, study plans or timetables, visit the support staff in the **Library Foyer** (ITMS, Student Central and Library staff are based there).

alternatives: how to set up my student login
I can't log in, my account isn't activated
where do I activate my student email
how do I get my username and password
How do I activate my computer account?
faqs.answer:
Go to **activation.cdu.edu.au** and step through the prompts. The New to CDU page also has the full set of steps.

If you get stuck, the support staff in the Library Foyer can help you one-on-one.

faqs.question: What do I need to do to set up IT access?
alternatives: how do I set up multi-factor authentication
authenticator app setup for my student account
faqs.answer: After activating your account, set up **Microsoft Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)**. This keeps your account secure, and you'll need it to sign in to CDU systems and the CDU app.

alternatives: where do I get my student ID card
how to get my ID card

faqs.question: How do I apply for a USI?
alternatives: what is a unique student identifier
where do I enter my USI
faqs.answer:
Getting a **Unique Student Identifier (USI)** is quick, easy and free.

1. Have a valid form of ID ready.
2. Create your USI on the USI Registry System.
3. Enter your USI in **My Student Info**, under Enrolment Steps.

Your USI is needed for CDU's government reporting, and for international students it also matters for visa compliance.

faqs.question: As an international student, what do I need to update in My Student Info?
alternatives: which address do I put in my student info
do I need a semester address
faqs.answer:
Please check your details in **My Student Info**. It's vital for CDU's government reporting and your visa compliance.

- **Contact Details:** enter your **Australian address**.
- **Home Address and Emergency Contact:** enter your **home-country address** and an emergency contact number.
- The Semester Address is **not** compulsory.

Also make sure your **USI** is entered under Enrolment Steps.

faqs.question: How can I get help with accommodation?
alternatives: find a place to rent in Darwin
faqs.answer:
Start at CDU **Accommodation Services**. Options include:
- **CDU Village:** join the waitlist for a long-term room.
- **Study Stays:** CDU's off-campus listings (usually shared houses or granny flats). Only CDU students can view it.
- **Unilodge** near Casuarina Shopping Centre (shared accommodation).
- **Homestay:** Global Experience or Australian Homestay Network, for short stays of up to about 8 weeks.
- General sites: **Flatmates.com.au**, **realestate.com.au**, **Gumtree** and the Facebook group *Buy Swap Sell Wanted Darwin*.
- **Airbnb** works as a temporary option but is expensive, especially in the dry season (May to October).

faqs.question: I have a driver's licence. Can I drive in the Northern Territory?
alternatives: can I drive with my foreign license
faqs.answer:
You can drive in the NT on your overseas licence for a **limited time**.

- If your licence isn't in English, you need an **International Driving Permit**, or an official English translation from an authorised translator in the NT. Carry it with your licence whenever you drive.
- If you stay in the NT **for more than 3 months**, you must transfer to an **NT driver licence**.

faqs.question: How many units do I need to enrol in to keep my Global Merit Scholarship?
alternatives: how many credit points per semester
faqs.answer:
Enrol in at least **80 credit points per year** (in line with student visa conditions), usually **40CP each in Semesters 1 and 2**, unless you have an approved **Reduced Study Load**.

If you can't take a full load (for example, because of a Learning Management Plan restriction), request a Reduced Study Load **before the deadline** and get approval from CDU Global.

faqs.question: If I fail a unit, do I lose my scholarship?
faqs.answer:
Not for a first fail. To keep the GMS you need to maintain **satisfactory academic progress**, or have a **Learning Management Plan** in place and seen by CDU Global.

- After a first fail, plan how to repeat the unit or find another pathway, especially if it's a core unit.
- Repeated fails can lead to an Under Review or Under Progression notice. If you're contacted by the Progression team, **respond and follow their guidance**.
- You may lose eligibility if you don't show improvement or don't tell CDU Global your plans.

faqs.question: How can I transfer my EndNote Library to another computer?
faqs.answer:
To move your EndNote Library to another location, you need to first compress the original EndNote Library or Groups of the Library you want to move.
1. Compress your EndNote Library file:
Open the EndNote Library.
Go to File and select Compressed Library (.enlx).
In the dialogue box that appears, you can choose to either Create or Create & Email.
Select whether to create With File Attachments or Without File attachments.
Click Next (Windows) or OK (Mac) and save it at your desired location.
2. Move the compressed file to the second computer:
Option 1: Email the zip file to yourself.
Option 2: Use cloud storage service such as OneDrive if the zip file is too big to email.
Option 3: Transport the zip file using a flash drive.

There's more detail on the page below.

faqs.question: How do I create a Hanging Indent?
faqs.answer:

The APA reference style uses hanging indents in the references. The hanging indent is 5-7 spaces (1.27cm in a Word document).
For example:
Roitman, J. L., & La Fontaine, T. P. (2012). The exercise professional’s guide to optimizing health: Strategies for
preventing and reducing chronic disease. Wolters Kluwer Health.

faqs.question: What is a DOI and where can I find it?
faqs.answer:
DOI stands for Digital Object Identifier. It is a unique address for an online resource, just like a URL.
Many electronic resources (esp. journal articles) have a DOI. The location of the DOI may vary depending on the type of database you are using, however you can usually find the DOI on the first page of the article or database. See below for some examples:
In APA 7th ensure you format your DOI this way (incl. hyperlink): https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mnl.2011.07.013
If the DOI on your resource shows in the old format, as in the examples above, change the DOI as follows:
Old DOI format: DOI:10.1016/j.mnl.2011.07.013
New DOI format: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mnl.2011.07.013 (removing 'DOI:' and replacing it with 'https://doi.org/').

faqs.question: How do I back up my library in EndNote?
faqs.answer:
To back up your library in EndNote, there are two options:
Option One
To use the 'Save a Copy' command to create an exact copy of your library. Here are the steps:
With a library open, choose Save a Copy from the File menu.
Choose where to save it.
Click Save.
The new library does not open, it is simply saved to disk.
Option Two
To use the Compressed Library command to save a copy of your library and.data folder together in a compressed file (.enlx) which can be restored later in EndNote.
From the File menu, select Compressed Library (.enlx) and then Create.
Select the folder or drive where you are saving which will then give you a Compressed EndNote Library (filename.enlx).

faqs.question: Why do author names change in EndNote?
faqs.answer:
If you are referencing a corporate author using EndNote, you need to put a comma at the end of the author so that EndNote recognises it as a corporate author and doesn't move any words around.
For example, referencing the author Department of Education in EndNote, it should be entered as:
Department of Education,
If there is already a comma in the name you need to put a second comma
E.g.
Department of Education, Northern Territory should be:
Department of Education,, Northern Territory
For more information, read this article from EndNote
If you have any concerns or other difficulties, contact us.

This grade indicates you have received a written extension for a period of up to three months from the end of the semester (teaching period) to submit outstanding assessment items toward the final grade for the unit.
'NA' - Not Available
This grade is an administrative grade only and is issued where the unit lecturer has not yet provided the grade to be applied to your record. As soon as the grade is received, it will be entered and you can view your grade under the 'My Results' link in your My Student Info portal.

faqs.question: How is a course Grade Point Average (GPA) calculated?

The standard formula for calculating a course GPA at CDU is:
GPA = Total (achievable credit points x grade GPA value) / Total (achievable credit points)
GPA Value
HD, High Distinction, 7

faqs.question: How much does a degree cost?
faqs.answer:
Want to study, but think you can’t afford it? You needn’t feel like this because there are plenty of options to manage your uni expenses, so let’s crunch the numbers.
Course fees are the largest expense when studying: a course is broken down into individual units that each have an associated fee. A typical three-year degree normally consists of 24 units, with your fees calculated by semester based on the number of units you are enrolled in.
Check out the fees and payment page for a run-down of how much your units cost and information on Student Services and Amenities Fees.
There are a few different options for managing this expense:
Pay your fees in full each semester and you might be able to claim it at tax time.

Ask the Library or Student Central for the full details.

faqs.question: Do I have to study on campus, or are online options available?
faqs.answer:
We absolutely get that you’re probably going to need to balance study with your other commitments, like work, friends and family, so that’s why we offer more than 100 courses online. Studying online as an external student at CDU allows you to learn at your own pace, so you can study where and when it suits you.
You can also take advantage of other flexible learning options to suit your lifestyle, with the majority of our degrees offered part-time. We also offer a Summer Semester, so you can spread your study load across three semesters, which means you can shorten the time it takes to complete your degree. Here are some other clever ways to complete your degree sooner.

Ask the Library or Student Central for the full details.

faqs.question: Am I eligible to study at uni?
faqs.answer:
This is a great question! CDU’s admission requirements depend on the level of study you want to undertake, whether it’s a Vocational Education and Training course, or an undergrad or postgrad degree.
If you are looking at studying an undergrad degree with CDU, there are several ways to meet the admission requirements:
An Australian Tertiary Admissions Rank (ATAR) of at least 60 after any applicable adjustments have been applied.
Successful completion of a national vocational education and training qualification at Certificate IV level or higher. It’s important to note that some courses may require a minimum of a Diploma.
Successful completion of at least 0.5 year of full-time study (or equivalent) of a higher education degree/diploma.

faqs.question: I am renting for the first time. What do I need to know?
faqs.answer:
Before looking at rentals/student accommodation make sure you do a budget on your income and expenses. Study Australia provide useful information on studying, working and living in Australia. There is also a Living Costs Calculator that can help with your preparations. Apart from the rent, there will be other household expenses, such as electricity, internet, food, phone, clothes, fuel, entertainment etc.
Once you have organised your budget and are sure of your weekly budget, check in with individual real estate agents, www.realestate.com.au, newspaper The NT News (Wednesdays and Saturday editions), CDU StudyStays, Gumtree, and various Facebook rental/lease breaks pages to look at your options for accommodation.

There's more detail on the page below.

faqs.question: Does the off-campus accommodation service check the property, the landlord and any people living in the property?
faqs.answer:
No - Accommodation Services do not check any properties listed on CDU StudyStays.
CDU Off-Campus Accommodation Officers can provide students with the resources to find and inspect properties independently. We can check your lease, application forms, and provide advice if you experience any tenancy problems. Unfortunately, we can’t find, inspect or submit applications for properties on your behalf, as it is important that you inspect the properties to find the one that is right for you.

Ask the Library or Student Central for the full details.

faqs.question: Why are database listings still displayed when the accommodation provider tells me the vacancy has been rented?
faqs.answer: Providers sometimes forget to let us know their vacancy has been filled. The property may also have just been rented so providers have not had a chance to tell us or take down the advertisement. If you do come across a property that has been filled, but is still on our site as vacant please let us know!

faqs.question: If I have problems with the landlord, Real Estate Agent or other members of the household, what should I do?
faqs.answer:
You should always do as much research as you can about your rights and responsibilities before you sign a lease agreement or related documents.
If you need general, non-urgent advice about renting including your responsibilities, rights and the laws relating to renting and accommodation in Darwin, you can reach out to NT Consumer Affairs and Darwin Community Legal Service

faqs.question: Am I studying full-time or part-time, and how many units should I take?
alternatives: how do I know if I'm full time or part time
how many units is full time

do I enrol for the whole year or just the semester
faqs.answer:
Usually **2 units or fewer** in a semester is **part-time**. A full-time load is more than that, typically **4 units** per semester.

To check your study load, log in to the **CDU Portal**, then go to **My Apps > MyStudentInfo > Enrolment**. You only need to enrol for the **upcoming semester**, not the whole year.

Study plans work for part-time study too. If you're not sure which units to pick, contact **Student Central** on **1800 061 963**.
